newsitem.title: UK: Clinton, Blair to hold first talks end-May.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Blair to hold first talks end-May.

text.p: New British Prime Minister Tony Blair will have his first face-to-face talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton during an international meeting in the Netherlands on May 28, a government spokesman said on Sunday.
"The two men agreed they should meet as soon as possible and this will take place at the Netherlands meeting at the end of May," he said by telephone.

The meeting, to be held in the Hague, will commemorate the 50th anniversary of the U.S. Marshall Plan which pumped billions of dollars into western Europe after World War Two to help rebuild the shattered continent.

But the government spokesman could not confirm a report in the Sun newspaper which said Clinton would then fly to London for more talks with the new British prime minister, who won a crushing election victory last week.
Western diplomats said the likelihood of a Clinton-Blair meeting in London depended on whether a NATO-Russia summit went ahead as planned on May 27.

"The chances are that Clinton will only want to do two things in Europe, so if the NATO-Russia summit is on and Clinton then goes to the Hague it's less likely he would then fly to London to talk to Blair," said one.
A White House spokesman said last week that the U.S. government wanted to see a continuation of the good relations between the two NATO members.

The U.S. media has sometimes portrayed Blair as a Clinton "clone", focusing on the similarities between the two. Both are relatively young politicians who sought to move their parties from the left of the political spectrum to the centre.
Some strategists from Clinton's Democratic Party discreetly advised the Labour team in the run-up to the election.
